title: Torsion en cohomologie cristalline : notes manuscrites (s.d.), copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (section 8.5). X is a smooth projective variety of dimension n over a field k of characteristic p, embedded in P^r_k. Y = X ∩ H is a smooth section by a hypersurface of degree d, so dim Y = n-1.

E(Y) is the 'vanishing' (evanescent) part of the crystalline H^{n-1}(Y/W), viewed as a motif with Frobenius. E(Y,O_Y) is the corresponding vanishing part of H^{n-1}(Y,O_Y), with its p-linear Hasse–Witt operator. The subscript ss denotes the semisimple (stable) part on which that operator is bijective.

The exact sequence (8.5.1) links (E(Y)⊗_W k)_ss to E(Y,O_Y)_ss through a map φ, with correction maps v and w built from the cohomology and p-torsion of X. It gives inequality (8.5.6): dim(E(Y)⊗k)_ss ≥ dim E(Y,O_Y)_ss, up to a correction (-dim Ker w, or -t^{n-1}(X,p)) that is crossed out in the final version.

dim(E(Y)⊗k)_ss is the number of Frobenius eigenvalues on the vanishing cohomology that are p-adic units, i.e. the slope-0 (unit-root) multiplicity. Section 8.5.8 (previous page) shows this number is constant on an open set U_d of the linear system.

This page:
- Goal: show that for d large this number is nonzero. That implies — and Grothendieck says it is 'sans doute équivalent' — that E(Y) has maximal 'niveau' n-1. In modern terms the motif is not a Tate twist, i.e. it has Hodge coniveau 0, so h^{0,n-1} of the vanishing part is nonzero.
- By (8.5.6) it suffices that the generic value of dim E(Y,O_Y)_ss be positive (the hatched word may have been 'tends to +∞') as d → ∞. In words: the generic large-degree section has nonzero stable Hasse–Witt rank on its vanishing H^{n-1}(O).
- A marginal note says this is established in n°7. The crossed-out sentence suggests n°7 also gave φ ≠ 0 under a bound on the semisimple p-torsion of X.

8.5.9 (k arbitrary, even imperfect):
- U_d is the open set of hypersurfaces of degree d whose section with X is smooth of dimension n-1 and whose E(Y,O_Y)_ss has maximal rank.
- Over U_d the sequences (8.5.1) glue to an exact sequence of locally free modules with semisimple p-linear operator.
- By 8.4.2 (the Lang/Katz-type equivalence between such modules and étale F_p-local systems), this is an exact sequence of étale local systems of F_p-vector spaces.
- Equivalently, after choosing a geometric point, it is an exact sequence of finite-dimensional F_p-representations of G = π_1(U_d).
- The map φ goes from the local system of the E(Y)⊗_W k' to that of the E(Y,O_Y), with constant kernel (coming from X, hence from k).
- For k finite one may enlarge k so that Frobenius acts with eigenvalues 1 on H^n(X,O_X)_ss, hence on the constant part.

Next page: the variation, as Y moves in U_d(k'), of the mod-p unit-root Frobenius eigenvalues of E(Y) is then described entirely by the F_p-monodromy representation of π_1(U_d) on the stable Hasse–Witt part, together with the Chebotarev distribution of Frobenius elements.

Purpose: a mod-p, unit-root analogue of Lefschetz-pencil monodromy theory, aimed at controlling ordinary (unit-root) eigenvalues and p-torsion in crystalline cohomology of hypersurface sections.
errors: 'sans doute équivalent': in general, maximal level (h^{0,n-1} ≠ 0) does not imply a nonzero unit-root part (e.g. supersingular elliptic curves). The equivalence can only hold generically in this specific family; it is consistent with, and was later secured by, generic ordinarity of complete-intersection sections (Deligne, Illusie 1990).

Logical gap: if the correction term (dim Ker w or t^{n-1}(X,p)) is kept in (8.5.6), positivity of dim E(Y,O_Y)_ss is not enough. One needs it to exceed the bounded correction, e.g. dim → ∞; the hatched original may have said this. The final text deletes the correction without justification, relying on the conjectural Ker v = 0 / Ker w issues of 8.5.7.

The description of the kernel of φ as constant, and the reduction to eigenvalue 1 on H^n(X,O_X)_ss, depend on the unproven injectivity of v (8.5.7). The foundations of crystalline cohomology were not yet available, as the next page itself admits.

ideas.what: Nonzero unit-root (slope 0) part of the vanishing cohomology of a generic hypersurface section of large degree, deduced from positivity of the stable Hasse–Witt rank on H^{n-1}(Y,O_Y)
ideas.modern_name: generic ordinarity / generic nonvanishing of p-rank for hypersurface sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Miller (generic invertible Hasse–Witt, 1970s), Koblitz (curves), Deligne and Illusie ('Ordinarité des intersections complètes générales', 1990)

ideas.what: Unit-root part nonzero implies Hodge level maximal ('niveau n-1')
ideas.modern_name: slope 0 part versus h^{0,n-1}; easy case of Mazur's Newton-above-Hodge

ideas.what: Locally free modules with semisimple p-linear operator over a base, equivalent to étale F_p-local systems (cited as 8.4.2)
ideas.modern_name: Lang–Katz correspondence (unit-root F-modules mod p versus F_p étale local systems)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lang; Katz (SGA 7 / 'p-adic properties of modular schemes', 1973)
ideas.where_published: related material in SGA 4½ / SGA 7 (Katz exposés), not certain

ideas.what: Mod-p monodromy representation of π_1 of the space of smooth hypersurface sections on the stable Hasse–Witt / unit-root part of vanishing cohomology; Chebotarev governs the mod-p unit-root Frobenius eigenvalues
ideas.modern_name: mod-p (unit-root) monodromy of families, p-rank strata monodromy
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz (p-adic monodromy, unit-root F-crystals), Ekedahl (1987), Chai, Achter–Pries (curves)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, for an arbitrary smooth polarized X, the mod-p monodromy representation of π_1(U_d) (smooth degree-d hypersurface sections) on the unit-root / stable Hasse–Witt part of the vanishing cohomology. He proposes that it fully describes the variation of mod-p unit-root Frobenius eigenvalues. The 'big monodromy' question for this representation is not addressed here. In this generality — sections of an arbitrary X rather than moduli of curves or abelian varieties — it seems little studied.
missed.quote: une suite exacte de représentations de G = π_1(U_d) dans des vectoriels de dimension finie sur F_p
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a mod-p analogue of Deligne's Lefschetz-pencil monodromy (Weil II). Big mod-p monodromy results here would give equidistribution of unit-root Frobenius eigenvalues mod p for hypersurface sections. Such results exist for p-rank strata of M_g (Ekedahl, Achter–Pries) but are less developed for linear systems on general X.

missed.claim: This is an early (pre-Mazur, pre-Illusie) program linking p-torsion of the crystalline cohomology of X to generic ordinarity of its hypersurface sections. The correction terms (Ker w, t^{n-1}(X,p)) measure how the torsion of X obstructs transfer of Hasse–Witt rank to unit-root rank.
missed.quote: Sous la forme de (8.5.6), on voit que ceci est assuré dès que l'on sait que dim E(Y,O_Y)_ss > 0 pour d → +∞
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Illusie's generic ordinarity proof does not track torsion of the ambient X in this way. An explicit inequality involving torsion of X could still be informative.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains an unpublished early sketch of generic ordinarity of hypersurface sections and of a mod-p unit-root monodromy theory over the linear system, predating Mazur, Katz and Illusie. The main results were later obtained independently, so it is mostly historically notable rather than new.
